source_text: IV. Martianus ait: Aut sacrifica, aut morere. respondit Achatius: Haec et Dalmatae faciunt, latrocinandi arte callentes: ubi angustias viarum et secreta itineris loca obsederint ad necandum, venantur singulos transeuntes, et ubi quisque viator illuc pedem tulerit, hac pactione constringitur ut aut pecuniam relinquat aut vitam. nemo itaque ibi quid sit rationis interrogat, sed quid possit ille qui cogit. similis est tua sententia, qui aut iniusta impleri praecipis, aut minaris exitium. nihil formido, nihil timeo. ius publicum punit scortatorem, adulterum, furem, corruptorem sexus virilis, maleficum et homicidam. horum si reus sum, ante vocem tuam iam me ipse condemno; sin vero, eo quod deum qui est verus colo, ducor ad poenam; non legis, sed iudicis voluntate condemnor. propheta clamat interminans: Non est qui inquirat deum; omnes declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt. ideo purgare te non potes. scriptum est enim: Omnis in quo iudicat, sic et iudicabitur. et iterum: Ut iudicas, sic et iudicaberis, et ut facis, sic et erit tibi. Martianus ait: Ego non sum iussus iudicare, sed cogere. unde si contempseris, certus esto de poena. respondit Achatius: Et mihi praeceptum est ne quando deum meum negem. si servis homini fragili atque carnali cito ab hoc saeculo recessuro, quem mox a vermibus scis edendum, quanto magis ego potentissimo deo obedire debeo, cuius virtus constat in saecula? et cuius illud est dictum: Qui me denegaverit coram hominibus, et ego denegabo eum coram patre meo, qui est in caelis, cum venero in gloria et virtute praedicta iudicare vivos et mortuos.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus says: either sacrifice or die. Achatius answers: the Dalmatians, skilled by the art of robbing, do these things: when they have occupied narrows of roads and hidden places of a route for killing, they hunt single passers-by, and when any traveler has brought his foot there, he is bound by this bargain, that he leave either money or life. No one there asks what is of reason, but what he who compels is able to do. Your sentence is similar, you who order either unjust things to be fulfilled or threaten destruction. I fear nothing, I dread nothing. Public law punishes fornicator, adulterer, thief, corrupter of male sex, sorcerer and murderer. If I am guilty of these, before your voice I myself condemn me; but if because I worship God who is true I am led to punishment, I am condemned not by will of law but of judge. The prophet cries out threatening that there is none who seeks God and all have turned aside and together become useless. Therefore you cannot cleanse yourself. For it is written that everyone in what he judges, so also will he be judged. And again: as you judge, so also will you be judged, and as you do, so also will it be to you. Martianus says: I was not ordered to judge but to compel; hence if you despise, be certain of punishment. Achatius answers: and to me it was commanded never to deny my God. If you serve a fragile and fleshly man soon to depart from this age, whom you know soon to be eaten by worms, how much more ought I to obey the most powerful God, whose power stands unto ages, and whose is that saying that whoever will have denied me before men, I also will deny him before my Father who is in heaven, when I shall have come in foretold glory and power to judge living and dead.
pass_b_english: Martianus said, Either sacrifice, or die.

Achatius answered, The Dalmatian bandits do just this, for they are skilled in the art of robbery: when they have occupied the narrow defiles of the roads and the hidden spots along a route in order to kill, they hunt down each traveler one by one, and when any wayfarer has set foot there, he is trapped by this bargain, that he must leave behind either his money or his life.
There no one asks what reason demands, but what the man who uses force is able to exact.
Your sentence is like theirs, since you command either that unjust deeds be carried out, or you threaten ruin.
I am afraid of nothing, I dread nothing.
The public law punishes the fornicator, the adulterer, the thief, the corrupter of the male sex, the sorcerer, and the murderer.

If I stand guilty of these, I condemn myself even before you speak; but if I am dragged to punishment because I worship God who is true, then I am condemned not by the will of the law, but by the will of the judge.
The prophet cries out in warning, There is no one who seeks God; all have turned aside, together they have become worthless (Psalms 13:1-3).
For it stands written, In whatever a man judges, so also shall he be judged.
And again, As you judge, so also shall you be judged, and as you do, so also shall it be done to you.
Martianus said, I was not ordered to judge, but to compel; so if you show contempt, be certain of punishment.
Achatius answered, And to me it has been commanded never to deny my God.

If you serve a fragile and fleshly man who will soon depart from this age, whom you know will soon be eaten by worms, how much more ought I to obey the most powerful God, whose strength endures through the ages?

And his is that saying, Whoever shall have denied me before men, I also will deny him before my Father who is in heaven, when I shall come in the foretold glory and power to judge the living and the dead (Matthew 10:33).

lemmas.gloss: offer sacrifice to the gods here

choices.why: nominative subject of punit; general criminal law is meant, not a statute about Christians

choices.english: one who corrupts the male sex
choices.why: sexus virilis specifies the victim class, so it denotes pederastic corruption rather than adultery in general

choices.english: not by the will of the law, but of the judge
choices.why: genitives legis and iudicis depend on voluntate; the contrast is law versus personal will
rejected: not of law, but I am condemned by the judge's will
